nodes.question: Why is the issue of socioeconomic disparities important in the context of sustainability policies?
nodes.answer: Socioeconomic disparities complicate efforts to implement uniform sustainability policies as different groups prioritize their immediate economic needs over environmental concerns.
nodes.paragraph: Stable employment further reinforces this engagement by alleviating financial constraints and enabling long-term decision-making (Masson & Le mann, 2017). Conversely, lower socioeconomic groups often prioritize cost-saving measures over broader environmental efforts due to immediate economic needs and finan- cial constraints (Liu, 2010; Masson & Le mann, 2017). Limited access to environmental knowledge and education further hinders their capacity to engage in sustainable practices (Ivkovi & Mandi , 2024). These socioeconomic disparities are particularly relevant as the world grapples with persistent poverty and unprecedented economic growth in certain regions, complicating efforts to implement uniform sustainability policies. Standard instruments such as the New Ecological Paradigm (NEP) Scale and the Two Major Environmental Values (2-MEV) Scale have been widely used in environmental psy - chology to assess environmental perceptions (Manoli et al., 2019). While these tools pro- vide valuable insights, they often overlook the complexity introduced by socioeconomic variations, which play a critical role in shaping environmental attitudes. For example, the degree to which individuals prioritize environmental protection over economic growth may vary significantly based on their access to education, employment, and financial resources (Guo et al., 2024).
